sources.title: Treccani: Lucca, republic and duchy
sources.note: Institutional historical dictionary, 2010. Republic ended 1799, principality 1805, Bourbon duchy and cession to Tuscany 1847. No assumption that imported 1878 is sovereignty endpoint.

sources.title: Historical Archive of the Municipality of Lucca: institutional history
sources.note: Provincial archival catalogue. Changing governments 1799 to 1805, principality, Austrian provisional rule ending 1817, Bourbon duchy to 1847, later Tuscany and unification. Dates refer to actual exercise of rule rather than assigning full Bourbon government to Vienna 1815.

sources.title: Municipality of Lucca: map and chronology of the walls
sources.note: Official municipal visitor map: works concluded 1650; 1812 flood gates; Nottolini first public promenade 1818; Caffe delle Mura 1840. Only these dates used, not inconsistent wall heights.

sources.title: Italian Ministry of Culture: National Museum of Palazzo Mansi
sources.note: Description paragraphs: 1686 to 1691 renovation associated with Carlo Mansi/Eleonora Pepoli marriage 1688; music room by Dal Sole and Chiarini; silk merchants and embroidered satin alcove. Flemish tapestries installed late nineteenth century, so not treated as original seventeenth-century installation.

sources.title: Museo Galileo, Graziano Magrini: Nottolini Aqueduct
sources.note: Direct full text. Begun 1823, interrupted, completed 1851 after annexation. Guamo temple-cistern 1823 to 1825, filtering, arched conduit, San Concordio tank, iron pipes with movement allowed for temperature change, public fountains. Quotes from Mazzarosa 1843; cross-source attribution counted manually in handoff.

sources.title: Museo Galileo, Graziano Magrini: Liceo Classico Niccolo Machiavelli
sources.note: 1785 institution, 1790 chemistry instruments, 1819 reform and scientific collections. 28 February 1837 decree for free Sunday artisan instruction; subjects exact list. Later museum object totals not assigned to historical school.

sources.title: Museo Galileo, Elena Fani: Hospital of San Luca or della Misericordia
sources.note: Merchant guild administration until 1807, then princely patronage; separate wards and foundling accommodation. Medieval foundation date not required for mapped phase.

sources.title: Antonio Mazzarosa: Guida di Lucca e dei luoghi piu importanti del ducato, 1843
sources.note: ICAR digitized primary guide. Title/date verified against ICAR catalogue and indexed title leaf; printed page 81 hospital counts: 110 male and 137 female beds, separate medical/surgical teaching clinics eight beds each. Only main ward counts used. Combined attribution with aqueduct paragraphs remains below 200.

sources.title: Italian national cultural-property catalogue: Lucca soldo, eighteenth century, 0900598817
sources.note: Full institutional indexed linked-data record checked at dati.beniculturali.it/lodview-arco/resource/NumismaticProperty/0900598817.html. Eighteenth century; crowned shield with band LIBERTAS, reverse saint carrying city. Query exact inventory number plus LIBERTAS. No specific mint year invented.

sources.title: Canadian Institute of Ukrainian Studies: Pechenegs
sources.note: Used only for confederation, Don to Danube range, 972, 1036, 1091 and 1122 political changes and later service. Unsupported population/army totals, universal religious claims and rigid ethnic strata omitted.

sources.title: Aleksander Paroń: The Pechenegs, 2021
sources.note: Brill scholarly monograph, translation Thomas Anessi, entire work one budget. Printed pp 162, 165 to 166 and 174; PDF indices printed page plus 12. Seasonal movements and household craft discussed using comparative pastoral evidence, explicitly framed as reconstruction. Bone bow plates archaeological.

sources.title: Constantine VII: De administrando imperio, Greek text
sources.note: University of the Aegean Digital Patrology transcription, 2006, of medieval Greek work. Chapter 2, PDF page 2, Greek heading and cattle/horses/sheep trade and river portages; chapter 6, PDF page 3, negotiated remuneration including pepper. Modern transcription, not photograph of a tenth-century manuscript or Pecheneg-language text.

sources.title: Florin Curta: The Image and Archaeology of the Pechenegs, Banatica 23, 2013
sources.note: Printed pp 159 to 161 and 168 to 170. Histria grave excavated 1972, cited eleventh-century report, 11 glass beads and two leaf-shaped pendants; Varna lead casting model and debated ethnic attribution. Entire paper, including other republications, one budget.

sources.title: Rosen Ivanov and Rumen Ivanov: Pecheneg Pottery from Bulgaria, 2024
sources.note: Plovdiv Historical Forum VIII/2, printed p 19 abstract. Predominance of kitchenware over tableware, northeastern 1030s to 1040s and southeastern mid/later eleventh-century material. Attribution belongs to authors, not assumed ethnicity of every vessel. Full publisher PDF accessible, repository abstract independently checked.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Six imported snapshots 1650 to 1878, bbox approximately 10.2619 to 10.7515 E, 43.578 to 44.1413 N, city and surrounding territory. Historical phases separated; post-1847 label explicitly warns independence ended. No successor links invented without root geometry review. Mansi late-nineteenth installation of Flemish tapestries omitted as anachronistic.

Imported world900 coverage 900 to 1000; bbox 31.49851 to 36.29376 E, 48.5810 to 50.72245 N. Small northern Dnipro-region fragment excludes much of historical Don-to-Danube range. Public warning explicit. No aliases or successors. Histria/Varna/Bulgarian pottery later context separately headed and dated; no invented midpoint item.year values. Greek sample is external testimony, not Pecheneg writing.
